question: Will this stop the shadow fleet, yes or no?

lines.text: Royal Marines have landed on the Faroe Islands.
The first time British forces have trained there since the Second World War.
lines.note: GOV.UK: first Royal Marines exercise in the Faroes since WWII

lines.text: Alongside Danish forces, they practised amphibious landings and boarding ships at sea.
One boarding drill used a Faroese fishing boat, the Gotunes.
It's part of Britain's Exercise Lion Protector, from the North Atlantic to the Baltic.
The Telegraph says the target is Russia's shadow fleet: tankers moving sanctioned oil.
Britain sanctioned eight more shadow fleet ships just yesterday.
In June, British forces first stopped a shadow fleet tanker in the Channel.
Defence Secretary Wes Streeting says these waters are the front line.

scene.quote: The North Atlantic, High North, and Baltic are the frontline of the UK's security

lines.text: The First Sea Lord says: that is what credible deterrence looks like.

scene.quote: That is what credible deterrence looks like.
scene.who: Gen Sir Gwyn Jenkins, First Sea Lord

lines.text: In April 1940, 193 Royal Marines landed here, days after Germany invaded Denmark.
lines.note: Wikipedia: Operation Valentine, 13 Apr 1940, 193 Royal Marines

lines.text: Ministers from the ten-nation Joint Expeditionary Force are meeting in Iceland.
Back on the Faroes after eighty years. Will this stop the shadow fleet, yes or no?
